intro: Buying a $425,000 home in Buffalo can involve a very different financial commitment from purchasing a similarly priced condominium in New York City. Local property taxes, building maintenance fees, insurance premiums and financing requirements can significantly affect your monthly housing expenses.

Our free New York mortgage calculator helps you estimate these costs before purchasing a property. Enter your home price, down payment, interest rate and loan term, then include property taxes, homeowners insurance and applicable fees to establish a realistic homebuying budget.

sections.heading: Understanding the New York Housing Market

blocks.markdown:
New York offers housing opportunities across metropolitan neighborhoods, suburban communities, university towns and rural regions.

According to the [US Census Bureau's New York housing statistics](https://www.census.gov/quickfacts/fact/table/NY/HSG860224), the median value of owner-occupied housing was $423,800 during the 2020–2024 survey period.

Median selected monthly ownership costs among households with mortgages were $2,555, while the homeownership rate was 54.3%.

These historical statistics do not represent current property asking prices.

Homes in Manhattan, Brooklyn, Long Island and Westchester County may have substantially different prices from properties in Buffalo, Rochester, Syracuse or Albany.

Research recent comparable sales within your preferred neighborhood. Consider transportation expenses, local property taxes and association fees alongside the purchase price.

sections.heading: How to Use the New York Mortgage Calculator

blocks.markdown:
Begin by entering your expected property purchase price and available down payment.

Select a repayment period and enter your lender's quoted annual interest rate. You can consult [Freddie Mac's mortgage market survey](https://www.freddiemac.com/pmms) for a national benchmark if you have not received a quote.

Next, enter annual property taxes, homeowners insurance and monthly association fees.

Include private mortgage insurance if your conventional financing requires it.

Review the estimated monthly housing payment and adjust individual inputs to compare different borrowing arrangements.

The amortization schedule helps you understand how your outstanding mortgage balance decreases over time and how much interest you could pay.

Our national Mortgage Calculator also allows you to compare financing scenarios outside New York.

sections.heading: How New York Property Taxes Affect Your Mortgage

blocks.markdown:
New York property taxes depend on local assessments, applicable exemptions and tax rates established by taxing jurisdictions.

The [New York Department of Taxation and Finance's assessment guidance](https://www.tax.ny.gov/pit/property/learn/howassess.htm) explains that municipalities may assess properties at full market value or a percentage of market value.

New York City and Nassau County also operate property classification systems with different assessment arrangements.

### New York property tax calculation example

Suppose a home has a market value of $425,000, but its taxable assessed value is $300,000.

Assume a hypothetical combined property tax rate of $24 per $1,000 of taxable assessed value.

Actual property taxes may include separate county, municipal, school district and special district charges.

Review the state's [property tax calculation guidance](https://www.tax.ny.gov/pit/property/learn/proptaxcalc.htm) and obtain a property-specific estimate from your local assessor.

### New York City property taxes

New York City uses four property tax classifications.

According to the [NYC Department of Finance](https://www.nyc.gov/site/finance/property/property-determining-your-assessed-value.page), Class 1 properties generally use a 6% assessment ratio, while Classes 2, 3 and 4 generally use 45%.

Class 1 includes most one- to three-family homes.

Annual assessment limitations may prevent the actual assessed value from reaching the amount produced by applying the standard ratio.

sections.heading: New York STAR Property Tax Relief

blocks.markdown:
The School Tax Relief program, commonly called STAR, provides qualifying homeowners with assistance toward school property taxes.

### Basic STAR

Eligible homeowners with qualifying income of $500,000 or less may receive the Basic STAR credit.

Ownership, principal residence and income requirements apply.

### Enhanced STAR

Enhanced STAR provides additional benefits to qualifying older homeowners.

The published income limit for 2026 benefits is $110,750. For 2027 benefits, the limit increases to $113,550.

At least one resident owner generally must meet the applicable age requirement of 65.

Review the [official STAR eligibility requirements](https://www.tax.ny.gov/pit/property/star/eligibility.htm) before assuming eligibility.

New homeowners generally register for the STAR credit instead of the older STAR exemption program.

The credit is paid directly to qualifying homeowners rather than automatically reducing their school tax bills. Consequently, it should not automatically be deducted from monthly mortgage escrow estimates.

Visit the [STAR registration portal](https://www.tax.ny.gov/pit/property/star/) after establishing the property as your primary residence.

Insurance premiums depend on your property's construction, replacement cost, location, condition and selected coverage.

New York homeowners may face coastal storms, flooding, freezing temperatures and other weather-related risks.

Obtain property-specific insurance quotes before finalizing your purchase.

### Hurricane and flood insurance

Properties along Long Island, coastal New York City and waterfront communities may have additional insurance considerations.

The [New York Department of Financial Services](https://www.dfs.ny.gov/consumers/help_for_homeowners/insurance/basic_coverage) explains that some policies contain separate hurricane deductibles.

Standard homeowners insurance also generally excludes flooding.

Check your property's exposure through the [FEMA Flood Map Service Center](https://msc.fema.gov/portal/home).

Include any applicable additional insurance premiums in your mortgage calculator inputs.
The following estimates assume 20% down, a 6% fixed annual interest rate and a 30-year mortgage.
These examples exclude property taxes, insurance, PMI and association fees.

The State of New York Mortgage Agency, commonly known as SONYMA, provides mortgage financing and purchase assistance through participating lenders.

### SONYMA mortgage programs

SONYMA's primary financing options include Achieving the Dream and the Low Interest Rate Program.

Eligible applicants may qualify for fixed-rate mortgages with relatively small down payment requirements.

Income limits, property price restrictions and borrower contribution requirements depend on the selected financing arrangement.

Review the [SONYMA preparation and eligibility guide](https://hcr.ny.gov/preparation-eligibility) before applying.

### DPAL Plus 2026

SONYMA launched an enhanced down payment assistance program on July 1, 2026.

The [DPAL Plus 2026 program](https://hcr.ny.gov/node/78501) offers eligible borrowers assistance of up to $30,000 toward qualifying purchase expenses.

Applicants must satisfy a household income ceiling of 60% of area median income.

Funding is limited and distributed to eligible borrowers while available.

The associated first mortgage interest rate generally increases by 0.40 percentage points when DPAL financing is attached, although certain specialized programs are exempt.

Compare your mortgage payment with and without assistance to understand the long-term borrowing costs.

sections.heading: Buying a Condominium or Co-op in New York

blocks.markdown:
Condominiums and cooperative apartments can involve expenses that differ from ordinary single-family homeownership.

Condominium owners generally pay common charges for shared building expenses and may receive individual property tax bills.

Cooperative apartment owners typically pay monthly maintenance charges that may incorporate building property taxes, underlying mortgage expenses and other operating costs.

Co-op financing also involves purchasing shares in a cooperative corporation rather than acquiring conventional direct ownership of an apartment.

When using the calculator, avoid adding property taxes separately if they are already included in your cooperative maintenance fees.

Review building financial statements, reserve funds, financing requirements and potential special assessments before purchasing.

sections.heading: New York Mortgage Recording Tax and Closing Costs

blocks.markdown:
New York buyers should prepare for expenses beyond their down payment.

The [New York State guide for new homebuyers](https://www.tax.ny.gov/pit/property/new-homebuyers/) identifies mortgage recording taxes and other property transaction expenses.

Additional local mortgage recording taxes may apply in New York City, Yonkers and other jurisdictions.

Closing costs can also include legal fees, title services, inspections, appraisals and prepaid insurance.

These expenses are generally separate from your regular monthly mortgage payment.

sections.heading: How Much House Can You Afford in New York?

blocks.markdown:
Begin with reliable monthly take-home income and subtract existing financial obligations.

Use our [New York Paycheck Calculator](/calculators/new-york-paycheck-calculator/) to estimate income after payroll deductions and our [Debt to Income Ratio Calculator](/debt/debt-to-income-ratio-calculator/) to evaluate outstanding borrowing commitments.

Include commuting expenses, childcare, utilities, association fees and emergency savings.

Compare mortgage offers using the [Consumer Financial Protection Bureau's Loan Estimate guide](https://www.consumerfinance.gov/owning-a-home/loan-estimate/).

Choose a property whose complete ownership expenses remain manageable alongside your other financial priorities.

### How much is a mortgage payment on a $425,000 New York home?

With 20% down, a 6% fixed interest rate and a 30-year mortgage, monthly principal and interest would be approximately $2,038.47. Property taxes, insurance and applicable fees increase the total housing payment.

### Can New York homeowners reduce property taxes through STAR?

Eligible homeowners may receive Basic or Enhanced STAR benefits toward school property taxes. New buyers generally register for the STAR credit, which is paid directly rather than automatically reducing their property tax bills.

### Does New York offer $30,000 in down payment assistance?

Yes. SONYMA's limited DPAL Plus 2026 program offers eligible borrowers up to $30,000 toward qualifying purchase expenses. Income limits, funding availability and financing conditions apply.
